title: Is AT&T an Undervalued Dividend Stock to Buy for Passive Income Investors? | T Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; captions readable
summary: Parkevtate evaluates AT&T as a dividend opportunity for passive-income investors. The stock offers a ~4.36% yield — below 10-year government bond and money-market rates, but with capital-gains upside attached. The focused strategy (divestitures, debt paydown) shrank revenue from $185B to $127B, but organic growth is low-single-digit with mid-to-high-single-digit EPS growth expected from productivity gains; operating margin rose from 17.5% (2017) to 21%, helped by internal AI (open-source models cut AI costs ~90%). Concern: ROIC of 8.11% sits roughly at WACC — weak capital allocation — and a major 6G upgrade cycle is coming, requiring heavy investment from AT&T and Verizon. Forward PE of 9.9 is fair for a saturated market. Near-term catalyst: the foldable iPhone upgrade cycle driving customer engagement and accessory upsells. His DCF fair value is $34.60 vs $25.50 market price — undervalued on DCF, fairly valued on forward PE; comprehensively 'slightly undervalued to undervalued.' Verdict: BUY with medium conviction for dividend investors. Bull case: improving margins, accelerating profitability growth from 2028. Bear case: looming 6G capex with AT&T's weak capital-allocation record; 4.36% yield trails risk-free rates. Call: T BUY at $25.50 (DCF fair $34.60), medium conviction. No flip — no prior parkevtate call on T.
